title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and payload limits for OpenAI-compat function calls
author: Carlos Mendoza
description: Motivation: Production incidents over the past two weeks showed two recurring surface regressions: (1) high-latency requests for tool/function calling when payloads and structured outputs hit the streaming proxy buffer boundary, and (2) unexpected 413-style rejections when OpenAI-compat clients submitted larger function call payloads. This PR introduces coordinated runtime and gateway changes to reduce tail latency, preserve streaming semantics (including chunked function/tool call payloads), and maintain OpenAI-compat behavior for existing clients. Key changes: 1) Increase default streaming proxy write buffer from 64KB to 256KB with adaptive flush thresholds to reduce small-write syscalls while bounding memory per connection. 2) Introduce a routing rule override that pins tool/function-calling requests to low-latency routes when the request declares "openai_compat": true or when the route header indicates function_call lifecycle (preserves prior behavior for existing customers). 3) Add graceful fallback where very large single-message payloads are accepted but proxied with chunked transfer and backpressure signals to the runtime; clients receive consistent OpenAI-compatible status codes and structured output framing. 4) Add feature flag api.gateway.buffer_tuning.v2 for staged canary rollout and traceable metric tags. 5) Update e2e and integration tests to include large function_call payloads, streaming boundary tests, and a synthetic workload that reproduces prior incident latencies. Checklist: - [x] Buffer tuning implemented and feature-flagged - [x] Routing override for OpenAI-compat tool calls - [x] Chunked proxying with backpressure and canonical status mapping - [x] Tests added and flaky test fixes - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated (canary scope) - [x] Documentation PR queued for redwood-docs (link in commits) Risk and rollback: change is feature-flagged and controlled via a canary routing policy; rollback flips the feature flag and reverts buffer size via runtime config. Related: ENG-4821 performance investigation, SUP-913 customer report, DOCS-119 queued docs updates.
commit_summary: 3 commits: 1) gateway: add buffer tuning and adaptive flush thresholds; 2) routing: special-case openai_compat function_call routing and pin to low-latency pool; 3) tests/docs: add integration/e2e tests and docs pointer. Commits include unit tests for routing decision logic and mocked proxy behavior.

release_notes: Improves API Gateway streaming stability and OpenAI-compatibility for large function/tool call payloads; increases default streaming proxy buffer size with adaptive flush thresholds; introduces routing override for OpenAI-compatible function calls to reduce tail latency. Rollout is controlled by api.gateway.buffer_tuning.v2 feature flag.
